sections.html:
Moon Township is in western Allegheny County, on the south bank of the Ohio River, about 1,175 feet above sea level. It covers 24.1 square miles and had 27,261 residents in the 2020 census, and its ZIP code is 15108.

Six municipalities touch its borders, and across the river it faces three more:

  • Crescent Township to the north-northwest and the borough of Coraopolis to the north-northeast
  • Hopewell Township in Beaver County to the northwest
  • Findlay Township to the west and southwest, and North Fayette Township to the south
  • Robinson Township to the southeast, east and northeast
  • Edgeworth, Sewickley and Glen Osborne on the opposite bank, linked by the Sewickley Bridge

sections.h2: How did Moon Township get its start?
sections.html:
Moon was created in 1788 as one of the original townships of Allegheny County, and in 1789 it absorbed part of Washington County south of the Ohio River. At that point it covered roughly 145 square miles, and legend says a rider needed two days to cross it. Settlers kept asking for smaller units, so Fayette Township was cut away in 1790, followed by Findlay and Crescent townships. Beaver County later took the land north of the river.

The township stayed rural for almost two centuries. Population was 1,383 in 1850 and still only 2,900 in 1930. Then it jumped to 7,096 in 1950, 10,642 in 1960 and 18,317 in 1970, driven first by defense work and then by the airport.

The Mooncrest housing plan was built in 1943 for defense workers who made armor plate, munitions and ships at the nearby Dravo yard, and its homes were sold to private investors in the mid-1950s. A Cold War missile battery known as Nike Site PI-71 once stood here and is now a nature preserve.

sections.h2: How do the airport and the university shape Moon's housing market?
sections.html:
Pittsburgh International Airport opened in Moon in 1951 and turned the farm country of the western hills into a transportation crossroads, with Parkway West, I-376 and I-79 exits nearby. The passenger terminal later moved to neighboring Findlay Township in 1991, which cost Moon tax revenue, but a large share of the runways and the airport cargo area remain inside the township.

Moon is also home to the Air Force Reserve Command's 911th Airlift Wing, the Pennsylvania Air National Guard's 171st Air Refueling Wing and the National Weather Service forecast office for the Pittsburgh area. Robert Morris University has its main campus here, and University Boulevard is the township's business corridor, renamed in 2003. Walmart opened a supercenter on the former West Hills Shopping Center site in 2016.

Houses close to University Boulevard or the airport face different noise and traffic conditions than those on quiet interior streets.

sections.html:

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and how does it affect a Moon house?
sections.html:
Moon's 1991 to 2020 normals, from NOAA data, show a January daily high near 35.6 degrees and a low of 19.4, and a July high of 83.0 with a low of 62.2. Annual precipitation averages 41.80 inches, spread fairly evenly across the year, with roughly 2.6 to 4.4 inches in each month.

Winter temperatures hover around the freezing line and moisture arrives in every season. Features worth checking before you list include:

  • Roof condition and gutters, since water has to move off a hillside lot
  • Basement dampness and sump pump history
  • Retaining walls, steps and driveway surfaces that heave in winter
  • Furnace age and the efficiency of the heating system

A seller who has receipts for roof or drainage work on a hillside lot is in a better position than one who has none.

sections.h2: Does Moon Township regulate rental properties and historic homes?
sections.html:
Yes on both counts. Moon requires a rental inspection before each change of occupants. The township's rental packet asks for an inspection request form, an affidavit, an inspection agreement and a rental registration, with a $20 fee per unit. The Fire Marshal's office then schedules the appointment, and owners must report the names of all occupants within 30 days of move-in. A buyer who plans to rent the house after closing will need to go through that process.

The Mooncrest Historic District adds another layer. A property there needs a Certificate of Appropriateness before the township will issue a building permit, and the township's Mooncrest Historic Overlay Advisory Committee advises the Board of Supervisors on those certificates. Building permits are required for alterations, additions, porch roofs and sheds, and rules cover windows and doors along building fronts, dryer vents, coal chutes and roofing materials. The township office at 412-262-1700 can confirm whether an address is inside the district.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Moon sale?
sections.html:
The total realty transfer tax is 2 percent of the price for a house in Moon Township. Allegheny County lists a one-half percent township tax and a one-half percent Moon Area School District tax, and the state adds 1 percent. The county collects the tax at recording, with a separate check from the recording fees.

The county's own example shows how the math works: tax on a $40,000 house in Shaler Township is $800. By the same method, a $300,000 sale in Moon would produce $6,000 of transfer tax, split $3,000 to the state and $1,500 each to the township and school district. Family transfers can be exempt, and deeds that show no price need a Statement of Value.

Moon sellers who disagree with their assessment can use the county's Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review, which holds its hearings by telephone.

sections.h2: What are the options for a quick sale in Moon Township?
sections.html:
A fast sale usually depends on the house being ready for an inspection and a buyer who does not need a lender's timeline. Many owners compare these routes:

  • List the house and wait for an owner-occupant, which can bring the highest price when the home is in good shape.
  • Sell to a cash buyer that purchases as is, useful for estates, tenant-occupied houses or places that need repairs.
  • Sell to a neighbor, a relative or an investor you already know.

If the house is in the Mooncrest district or has rental history, gather the permits and inspection records first, since a buyer will ask for them.

faqs.q: Is Moon Township the same as Moon, Pennsylvania?
faqs.a: Yes. Moon Township is in Allegheny County and is the place most people mean. A separate Moon Township exists in Beaver County, so confirm the county when you search property records.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a house sale in Moon Township?
faqs.a: It totals 2 percent of the sale price: 1 percent to the state, one-half percent to the township and one-half percent to the Moon Area School District. Allegheny County collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental inspection to sell a Moon house with a tenant?
faqs.a: The township requires an inspection before each change of occupants, with a $20 fee per unit, plus a rental registration within 30 days of move-in. A buyer who keeps the tenant should ask whether the current paperwork is on file.

faqs.q: What is the Mooncrest Historic District?
faqs.a: It is a historic overlay area built in 1943 as defense worker housing. Owners need a Certificate of Appropriateness before a building permit is issued, and an advisory committee reviews requests.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Moon Township?
faqs.a: The Moon Area School District appears in the Allegheny County transfer tax table for Moon Township. Crescent Township also sits in that district, which helps when comparing nearby addresses.
